name: Teutonic Order
alt: monastic state of the Teutonic Knights

predecessors.name: Duchy of Masovia
predecessors.text: Chełmno Land (Culmerland), 'granting them Chełmno Land, or Culmerland, and any future conquests' (Golden Bull of Rimini, 1226)

predecessors.name: Livonian Brothers of the Sword
predecessors.text: the Swordbrothers' lands in Livonia, absorbed in 1237

successors.name: Duchy of Prussia
successors.text: the Order's remaining Prussian territories, secularized by Albert of Brandenburg

successors.name: Livonian Confederation
successors.text: the Livonian branch's lands (Latvia and Estonia)

ledger.x: 1230: the Teutonic Knights begin the Prussian Crusade from Chełmno Land, granted to them by the Golden Bull of Rimini.
1236: the Knights force most Pomesanians to submit.
1237: the Livonian Brothers of the Sword merge into the Teutonic Order.
February 1249: the Treaty of Christburg brings most Prussian tribes to peace.
January 1255: the Knights conquer Samland.
By 1277 the central Prussian tribes have surrendered.
13 November 1308: the Teutonic Knights take Gdańsk and with it Pomerelia.
1309: the Order's seat moves from Venice to Marienburg, the first seat of the Order inside the state's land.
September 1309: Brandenburg sells its claim to Pomerelia.
1329: the Order attacks Kuyavia and Dobrzyń Land in the Polish-Teutonic War.
1332: Kuyavia and Dobrzyń Land are in the Order's hands.
1332: the Order's conquest of Kuyavia and Dobrzyń is complete; the land is held, not fought over, until the 1343 peace.
16 May 1343: the Order takes the castles of Reval and Wesenberg in Danish Estonia.
8 July 1343: the Treaty of Kalisz returns Kuyavia and Dobrzyń to Poland.
1 November 1346: the contest over Estonia ends with the sale.
1 November 1346: the Order buys the Duchy of Estonia from Denmark.
1398: the Order takes Gotland from the Victual Brothers.
12 October 1398: the Treaty of Salynas gives Samogitia to the Order.
1402: the Neumark is pawned to the Order.
1408: the Order sells Gotland to Denmark.
May 1409: Samogitia rises against the Order.
1 February 1411: the First Peace of Thorn gives up Samogitia.
1 February 1411: the Peace of Thorn ends the fighting over Samogitia.
1422: Cliopatria sets the Livonian branch apart as its own state.
27 September 1422: the Treaty of Melno gives Nieszawa to Poland.
1454: the Order's seat moves from Marienburg to Königsberg.
February-March 1454: the Prussian Confederation rises and western Prussia turns to the Polish king.
1455: the Order sells the Neumark back to Brandenburg.
6 June 1457: Marienburg passes to the Poles.
19 October 1466: the Second Peace of Thorn ends the Thirteen Years' War.
19 October 1466: the Order gives up western Prussia.
1466: the Bishopric of Warmia passes to the Polish crown.
19 October 1466: the Order becomes a fief of the Polish Crown.
10 April 1525: the Order's fief ends in the Prussian Homage.
10 April 1525: the Order's Prussian state ends in the Prussian Homage.

wars.name: Prussian Crusade
wars.outcome: The Order conquered Prussia: Pomesania in 1233-36, the central tribes' peace at Christburg in February 1249, Samland in January 1255, the Great Prussian Uprising from 1260, Sudovia in summer 1283; 'the crusaders firmly controlled the Prussian tribes by the…

wars.name: Great Prussian uprising
wars.outcome: Crushed: 'The central Prussian tribes surrendered to the crusaders by 1277'.

wars.name: Livonian Order campaign against Novgorod (Battle on the Ice)
wars.outcome: 'In 1242, the Livonian Order tried to take the city of Novgorod' and Alexander Nevsky defeated them at the Battle on the Ice.

wars.name: Teutonic takeover of Pomerelia
wars.outcome: The Order took Gdańsk on 13 November 1308 and bought Brandenburg's claim for 10,000 marks in September 1309 (Treaty of Soldin).

wars.name: Polish-Teutonic War (1326-1332)
wars.outcome: The Order conquered Kuyavia and Dobrzyń Land 1329-1332; the Treaty of Kalisz of 8 July 1343 'formally concluded the Polish-Teutonic War, which began in 1326/1327' and returned both lands to Poland.

wars.name: Hunger War
wars.outcome: Named on the Polish-Lithuanian-Teutonic War page together with the Gollub War of 1422; no territorial change is stated.

wars.name: Polish-Lithuanian-Teutonic War
wars.outcome: Defeat at Grunwald (15 July 1410) after the Samogitian uprising of May 1409; the Peace of Thorn of 1 February 1411 had the Knights resign Samogitia for the lifetimes of Jogaila and Vytautas and cede the Dobrin Land, keeping 'essentially all' else.

wars.name: Gollub War
wars.outcome: Jogaila and Vytautas invaded in July 1422; the Treaty of Melno of 27 September 1422 gave Samogitia permanently to Lithuania and Nieszawa to Poland.

wars.name: Polish-Teutonic War (1431-1435)
wars.outcome: Ended by the Peace of Brześć Kujawski; no territorial result on the State page.

wars.name: Thirteen Years' War
wars.outcome: The Second Peace of Thorn of 19 October 1466: the Order lost Gdańsk Pomerania, Chełmno Land, Elbing and Marienburg and Warmia, and held eastern Prussia as a fief of the Polish crown.

certainty.note: Frontiers of conquest in the Prussian and Livonian wilderness and against Lithuania are approximate; the Polish frontier is sharp from the Treaty of Kalisz (8 July 1343) and the Peace of Thorn (1 February 1411).
The Lithuanian frontier was fixed by the Treaty of Melno (27 September 1422, 'unchanged for about 500 years') and the Polish one by the Second Peace of Thorn (19 October 1466).
